subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated `before_persistence_write` hook for durable state changes, or represent durable-write policy through enriched `before_tool_call` and provenance contracts instead?
rationale: This choice defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what plugins can see, whether they can block or mutate writes, and how failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Fold into existing policy hooks
options.body: Extend `before_tool_call` and related provenance/read-time APIs instead of adding a hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to provenance design
options.body: Keep this as a dependency of persistent-state provenance work until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, explicit block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest available history across Plugin SDK hook contracts, memory persistence, and the adjacent security-policy design referenced by the issue.
